channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Echoes Across Time · Mountain Artists Guild
item.description: The Mountain Artists Guild's winter juried show in Prescott, Arizona is mounted as a concert partnership with the Arizona Philharmonic, whose “Echoes Across Time” programme — Handel's Violin Sonata in D Major, Fazıl Say's Four Cities and Tchaikovsky's Piano Trio in A Minor — is the brief. Artists need not illustrate a particular composition; the brief is what the music awakens — a memory, a place, a person, a culture, a moment in history. The Guild suggests memory and nostalgia, childhood and family tradition, cultural heritage, remembrance, changing landscapes and cities, connections between generations, rhythm and movement, and music translated into colour, shape and texture. Photography is one of the two judged categories in its own right (“all types of photography mediums”), alongside original paintings; the show is 2D only, with no three-dimensional work, and reproductions, giclées and printed merchandise are excluded, as are nudes and work unsuitable for family viewing. CAUTION, TWO CONTRADICTORY ELIGIBILITY LINES ON ONE PAGE: the prospectus header reads “Open to members of Mountain Artists Guild only” and the fee table lists a member rate and nothing else, while a later paragraph reads “this exhibition is open to all artists”; the two sibling shows the Guild ran this year both printed a non-member rate as well, so the members-only reading is the one to plan around. Up to three works may be entered for the base fee, and members also agree to volunteer a minimum of four hours during the run or pay a $20 buyout. Entries are juried for the gallery show and then judged again in the gallery; the juror was still “TBA” when this entry was written. All artwork must be for sale, priced to carry the Guild's 25% member commission, and delivered in person — no shipping — with gallery intake on January 11, 2027. Canvas or frame size must be at least 154 square inches and no more than 1,728. The exhibition runs January 13 to February 14, 2027, award-winning work is shown at the February 14 concert at the Ruth Street Theater, and accepted entries stay in the online Web Gallery for three months. Note the cutoff is not end of day: entries close at 9 PM on January 2, 2027. — Deadline: January 2, 2027. Fee: $30 members only (first 3 works; Guild membership required, price not published). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Create! Magazine Issue #61 — Juried by Deep Space Gallery
item.description: Open call for Issue No. 61 of Create! Magazine, the artist-run print and digital publication, curated for the Winter 2027 issue by Deep Space Gallery in Jersey City. There is no theme this time — all subjects and media are welcome, photography among them — and the call is open to artists worldwide with no academic background required. Every entry goes to the gallery's curators, Jenna Geiger and Keith VanPelt, whose gallery has staged immersive installations at Spring/Break Art Fair during Armory Week, were one of 100 galleries invited into Artsy's inaugural FOUNDATIONS Winter 2024 showcase, and exhibited in PERSONAL STRUCTURES 2024: Beyond Boundaries at the European Cultural Centre during the 60th Venice Biennale. They choose one artist for the cover of the print and digital magazine; the cover artist also gets a feature spread inside the issue, an in-depth feature interview, an invitation onto the Create! Podcast and a free print copy. Additional selected artists receive a four-page spread in the print and digital editions, features across the magazine's website and social channels, and a complimentary digital issue with the option to order print. Submit up to 10 works — cohesive bodies of work and series encouraged — with a 300-word bio and a 300-word artist statement; the standard entry fee of $35 covers three images, with additional fees only if you choose to submit extra images or request an online interview. Artists retain full copyright, and there are no further fees if published. Jurying starts in December 2026, winners are announced in January 2027 and the issue is released in Winter 2027. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $35 / 3 images. Prize: Cover feature + publication.

item.title: Women Street Photographers Annual Exhibition 2027
item.description: The Women Street Photographers annual exhibition, open worldwide to women and non-binary photographers of all ages, with no age gate and no nationality restriction. Seventy finalists are exhibited at El Barrio's Artspace PS109 in New York City from 9 to 19 April 2027 as part of the WSP Festival, and printing and framing for the exhibition are fully covered by the organiser. Leica Camera USA awards four cash grants of US$1,000 each. Selected photographers also get a dedicated profile on the Women Street Photographers website and features across WSP's platforms, which the organiser puts at over 200,000 followers. The jury is Kathy Ryan, for 39 years director of photography at The New York Times Magazine; Sarah Meister, executive director of Aperture and formerly 25 years at MoMA; and Sehin Tewabe, an Ethiopian photographer and co-founder of Artawi Gallery in Addis Ababa. The three of them choose the finalists and WSP founder Gulnara Lyabib Samoilova then curates the hang. Review is blind — each entry is assigned a number and judges see no names or personal details. Entry is single images only, made after 1 September 2020, in street photography, street portraiture or abstract street photography in public spaces anywhere in the world; film, digital and smartphone frames are all accepted, minimum 1500 px on the long side, JPG, sRGB. AI-generated images, multiple exposures, composites, watermarks, text and borders are all barred, as is work previously published on the WSP website. Photographers keep full copyright and WSP takes a non-exclusive right to exhibit and promote selected work. The fee is $15 per photo to a maximum of 25 photos per entry, with a bonus rung — submit 20 or more and five of the entries are free — and anyone wanting to send more than 25 must start a fresh submission. The organiser also offers fee waivers of up to two free entries to photographers who cannot afford the fee (New York City residents excluded) or who cannot pay by card because of US embargo restrictions — request the waiver form by email. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: $15/photo. Prize: 4 × $1,000 + exhibition.

item.title: 2026 KinoSaito Annual Community Art Benefit
item.description: KinoSaito's year-end community show, hung salon style in the former St. Patrick's School that houses the arts centre in Verplanck, on the Hudson an hour north of New York City. The open call is free — "There is no application fee to apply, though a suggested donation of $10 per applicant is greatly appreciated" — and the submission guidelines open on "All mediums may be accepted", so a photographic print is eligible on the organiser's own wording. The eligibility gate is physical rather than curatorial: accepted artists must transport their own work to KinoSaito and collect it again if it does not sell, so the organiser states that only artists within commuting distance of 115 7th Street, Verplanck, NY 10596 are eligible to submit. Artists at any stage of their careers are encouraged to apply, and the organiser frames the show as a way of highlighting the talent in its own community as the centre heads into a sixth year of operation. The page says each artist may submit up to two works and that a maximum of one will be selected, but the application form marks both image uploads as required, so have two pieces ready. Work must be ready to hang or display, no larger than 36 inches in any direction, and priced at no more than $3,000 — and it must be for sale, with the artist keeping 50% of the sale price and the other 50% going to KinoSaito as a donation from the artist. The exhibition runs 11–20 December 2026, with an opening reception and performance on 12 December from 4 to 7 pm. Artists are notified on 29 November; drop-off is 5, 6 and 7 December and pick-up 20, 21 and 22 December. KinoSaito's programmes are supported by the New York State Council on the Arts and ArtsWestchester. — Deadline: November 11, 2026. Fee: Free (suggested $10 donation). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Keyhole · Memento Mori Gallery & Tattoo
item.description: A themed group show at Memento Mori Gallery & Tattoo in Lakewood, Colorado, built on a single image: "What do you see when you look through the keyhole? Maybe it's a secret room, a forbidden world, a memory, a dream, a hidden self, or a future waiting to be discovered. Perhaps the keyhole represents curiosity, privacy, desire, access, exclusion, transformation, or the tension between what is revealed and what remains unseen." The gallery describes itself as a lowbrow/outsider contemporary art gallery in the 40West Arts District, on the art walk circuit and in the same shopping centre as Casa Bonita, with good foot traffic on First Fridays. 2D and 3D work is accepted at $30 per piece, up to two pieces per artist. Photographic work is eligible as a printed, properly framed or mounted object — the gallery will not display digital artwork unless it is printed and framed or mounted properly, and will not accept photographic work that depicts another artist's artwork, including street art, without that artist's express permission. Everything must arrive ready to hang, meaning hanging hardware already attached: hanging wire is preferred, no adhesive mounts, and work that is not ready to hang will be rejected at drop-off. All work must be for sale with 40% of any sale going to the gallery, and cannot be sold elsewhere for the run of the show. Copyright stays with the artist. Drop-off is 30 January 2027, the First Friday reception is 5 February 2027 from 6 to 9 pm, the show runs to 26 February and pick-up is 27 February. Out-of-state artists are responsible for shipping both ways. — Deadline: January 9, 2027. Fee: $30 per piece. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Big Sky · Webster Arts
item.description: A national call for art opening Webster Arts' 2027 gallery season in Webster Groves, Missouri: "Every sky can be big. Webster Arts invites submissions for our opening show of 2027, Big Sky — artists may submit 2D and 3D artwork that delves into the sights that stir our souls. From vast, natural geographies to constructed architectural skylines, whether mapping the terrains of our souls or the layouts of our living rooms, you are invited to explore the expanses of your world." Work should be original and completed within the last three years. The medium rule is an explicit affirmative with one exclusion — "The exhibit will consider artworks of all mediums except for video" — so photography is admitted by the rule rather than by silence. An independent juror selects the exhibition and two cash awards: $250 Best in Show and one $100 Award of Excellence. This is an in-person exhibition on view 8 January to 8 February 2027, with an opening reception on Friday 8 January at 6:30 pm; accepted work must be shipped to or dropped off at the gallery by 23 December 2026 and stay for the full run. Framed wall pieces must be wired and no larger than 48 x 48 inches, all wall works on paper must be framed, and three-dimensional work must not exceed 32 x 32 x 60 inches or 50 pounds. No reproductions, and work previously exhibited in any Webster Arts gallery is not eligible. Sales are encouraged, and Webster Arts retains a 30% commission on all gallery sales, with local sales tax charged on top and handled by the gallery. Webster Arts has run exhibits, workshops, a plein air event, an art fair and concerts for over twenty years. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: $25 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $250 + $100.

item.title: Cabin Fever 2027 · Cape Fear Studios
item.description: Cape Fear Studios' midwinter show in its Main Gallery in downtown Fayetteville, on display 22 January to 23 February 2027, with an opening reception and awards on 22 January from 6 to 8 pm. The prospectus is explicit on both counts that matter: "This is a non-juried exhibition and is open to all artists, 18 or older" and "MEDIA: All media accepted." Each artist may submit up to two original works completed in the last two years; work must not be copied from another artist or from published material, and must not have been previously exhibited in Cumberland County. Awards are cash — First Place $125 and two Honorable Mentions of $50 each — presented at the opening reception. 2D work may not exceed 40 x 40 inches including the frame and must be properly wired with picture wire and D rings or eye hooks (no saw-tooth hangers); 3D work must be ready to display and free of quality issues not integral to the piece. All entries must be for sale at the price listed on the entry form, no work may be withdrawn early, and the studio retains 30% commission on sales, with payment to the artist within 30 days of the close of the exhibit. ENTRY IS HAND-DELIVERED ONLY, in person at the gallery on 14, 15, 16 and 19 January 2027 — "No late entries will be accepted" — which in practice makes this a call for artists within reach of Fayetteville. — Deadline: January 19, 2027. Fee: $15 (1 piece) / $25 (2 pieces). Prize: $125 / $50 x2 + Exhibition.

item.title: Paradise After-Hours — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: A public art exhibition on billboard ad space in New York City, curated by photographer Olivia "LIT LIV" Morgan and opening 11 December 2026: "A call for artists documenting queer nightlife and queer art." SaveArtSpace frames the brief against a real pressure — "For years, queer nightlife has faced pressure from city and government offices to shut down the bars, dance halls, and clubs that serve as safe spaces for queer people to dance, perform, and be fully themselves. Venues close. The community keeps creating." The call invites artists who are documenting and preserving that world as it shifts and changes, and asks for work that shows the best of the community: "the joy of the dance floor, the bright lights, the feeling of being free and being seen. The culture the mainstream now borrows from was born in queer spaces like these. They can try to close our spaces, but we have always existed and we always will." Artists of all ages and talents may submit between 8 October and 2 November 2026. Selected work is placed on a billboard in New York, NY from 11 December 2026 and stays up for at least one month; the selected artist is announced after 16 November 2026. Fees go to producing the exhibition, including buying the billboard space, and are tax-deductible donations to SaveArtSpace, a 501(c)(3) non-profit founded in 2015 that works to put culture over commercialism in urban advertising space. The entry form is the binding prospectus and it settles three things the call page does not: media — "All art is accepted. Media NOT accepted: Corporate logos, personal advertising and videos. Please submit still jpegs only", so photography is eligible by the organiser's own enumeration; the real cap of ten images, at a maximum 2 MB each; and the closing clock time of 11:59pm on 2 November. The form also charges the stated donation plus card fees, so the amount actually taken at checkout is $36.92 for one to three images, rising to $108.45 for ten. — Deadline: November 2, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Billboard exhibition in New York City.

item.title: Winter Solstice 2026 — Annual Members Exhibition · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: The Griffin Museum's annual Winter Solstice members' exhibition fills the Main Gallery in Winchester, Massachusetts with unframed prints from the museum's membership — "a chance to gather the many perspectives of our community into a single, radiant show, and to send a little bit of art home with new collectors before the year closes." Last year the museum made room for over 300 prints, hung wall to wall, and it is asking its members to fill the gallery again. The show is deliberately built to be collectible rather than competitive: each member submits one unframed photographic print, no larger than 13 inches on the longest side, ready to hang with clips or pins or to sit on a pedestal, with a maximum price point of $250 — "We want to give you an opportunity to find a collector for your print, so that you make some holiday money, and a small portion is donated to the museum to support our end of year giving." Submissions open 1 October and run through the month of October; registration comes first, prints are shipped from 1 November and must reach the museum by 1 December. The exhibition opens 11 December 2026 with an artist reception on 12 December, and closes 10 January 2027, when print sales are finalised and payments made. Membership of the Griffin Museum is required to submit; the museum's own membership ladder prices Individual at $70 a year, Students & Educators at $35, Senior (65+) at $50 and Distance Member — which requires residence outside the New England states — at $50, with Family at $100. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free (Griffin membership required: $70/year, $50 outside New England, $35 student). Prize: Exhibition + print sales.

item.title: Thresholds · A Photographer's Place
item.description: A monthly juried show in Gallery X at A Photographer's Place in Raleigh, built around the threshold as "a place of passage: a boundary between one state and another, between arrival and departure, certainty and possibility. It is not simply a line that separates, but a space in which transformation can occur." The gallery asks photographers to consider the places, experiences and moments that exist between states of being — transition and liminality between interior and exterior, presence and absence, intimacy and distance, memory and experience, the known and the unknown. The threshold may be architectural or psychological, personal or collective, tangible or imagined; it may be marked by a dramatic event or exist in the quietest of gestures — a pause before leaving, a landscape at dusk, a body in transition, a familiar place rendered unfamiliar. Work that embraces ambiguity and resists easy definitions is explicitly welcomed, as are photographs that reveal thresholds, question them, cross them or linger within them. Selected work hangs in Gallery X at the front of the space from 6 November to 1 December 2026, with an opening reception on 6 November, and is then presented on the gallery's website to be viewed year-round. Up to 5 JPEGs, colour or black and white, minimum 3000 pixels on the longest side. Accepted artists may optionally have their work printed by the gallery on its Canon imagePROGRAF PRO-1100. — Deadline: October 22, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 5 images). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Open Theme: 2026 · Black Box Gallery
item.description: An open-themed juried group photo show at Black Box Gallery in Portland, Oregon: "Open to all themes and ideas, all styles and genres, all perspectives on crafsmanship and photographic creativity." The gallery names landscape, architecture, portraiture, documentary, fashion, still life, conceptual projects, street, colour and black and white, nature and night photography as all welcome. Juror Todd Johnson, the gallery's founder and director, selects 26 photographs for the physical show (1–25 December 2026), with a further 50 for the online gallery annex; all 76 are reproduced in a catalog available on Blurb Books. Black Box provides free printing, matting and framing for every selected work — archival inkjet on Epson Premium Luster in a colour-calibrated environment, presented in 18"x24" black frames with pre-cut white mats. Selected photographers supply a high-resolution TIFF or JPEG; the gallery prints one exhibition print only, and no sale or further printing happens without the photographer's prior consent. Exhibition prints are kept in the gallery flat files for two years to promote the photographer to collectors, curators and critics, then shredded. Entry is by email with a PayPal fee payment: up to 5 JPEGs, 1200 pixels on the longest side at 72 PPI, 5 MB or less each. Open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional. The gallery takes 50% commission on sales, and work does not have to be offered for sale. — Deadline: November 13, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 5 photos). Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: Seasons 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the seasons, running at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography from 4 to 28 March 2027. "Seasons come and go, but each season can have its own distinct look and feel" — from the greens of Spring to the blues and whites of Winter, the gallery says the palette of each season changes and in turn changes how we see the world around us, and it wants photography that highlights those distinct changes and how they affect the environment around us. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi, 3000 pixels minimum on the shortest side) by free file transfer — Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox — to the gallery's submissions address; attachments are discouraged because they compress the files, and all images should be sent together. Selected work is printed and displayed in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the gallery's website, and included in an exhibition catalogue. Selected participants also receive a digital certificate of participation before the exhibition opens, have their installed work photographed and filmed for the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers who are selected pay a £50 participation fee covering printing and installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image, and a discount is available to anyone selected for both March exhibitions. Acceptance notification is by 4 November 2026 and the payment deadline for selected photographers is 18 November 2026. Only selected photographers are notified. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Women in Photography 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Open-themed international photography exhibition for women photographers, running at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography from 4 to 28 March 2027. The gallery has marked International Women's Day for several years with a show of work by women photographers from across the globe, and says this year is no different: "Women in Photography is an open-themed exhibition, meaning any theme or genre of photography is accepted", so there is no subject brief to answer — only the work. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi, 3000 pixels minimum on the shortest side) by free file transfer — Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox — to the gallery's submissions address; attachments are discouraged because they compress the files, and all images should be sent together. Selected work is printed and displayed in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the gallery's website, and included in an exhibition catalogue. Selected participants also receive a digital certificate of participation before the exhibition opens, have their installed work photographed and filmed for the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers who are selected pay a £50 participation fee covering printing and installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image, and a discount is available to anyone selected for both March exhibitions. Acceptance notification is by 4 November 2026 and the payment deadline for selected photographers is 18 November 2026. Only selected photographers are notified. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Protest, Everything's Connected · Photobook Cafe & Rapid Eye Darkroom
item.description: The eighth quarterly open call from Photobook Cafe and Rapid Eye Darkrooms, in partnership with UNCLE, takes protest as its theme — "visible in the streets, in our homes, online, in landscapes, within communities and in the everyday choices we make", loud or quiet, collective or deeply personal. The call asks how photography can document, challenge and reimagine acts of resistance, solidarity and social change, and it is explicit about the range it wants: climate and environmental action, social justice and equality, anti-war and peace movements, Indigenous rights, feminist, LGBTQIA+ or disability rights activism, or any other movement advocating for change. Documentary, conceptual work, portraiture, landscape, still life, archival material and experimental image-making are all named as welcome, and the organisers say they particularly want work that moves beyond protest-as-event — the people behind movements, the spaces they occupy, the lasting effects of activism, the quieter forms of protest that go unseen. Work may be new or drawn from personal archives, analogue, digital or alternative process, taken anywhere in the world. Guest judges Rebecca Zephyr Thomas (who has photographed LGBTQ+ activists for Dazed and Ukrainian protesters for Elephant, and worked with the Green Party and Extinction Rebellion) and Jade Smith (a director, photographer and filmmaker whose practice centres on protest, community and social documentary) select 35 exhibiting photographers for a group show and zine launch at The Photobook UK Gallery on 11 November 2026, with Best in Show announced that evening at 19:30. Of the 35, ten receive a 30-minute one-to-one mentoring session on portfolio development, project direction and professional practice; three Best in Show photographers are invited into a Photobook UK Public Programme group exhibition in 2027 with select printing supported by Rapid Eye Darkrooms; and ten have their work shown in an UNCLE street gallery across London, taking the work out of the gallery and into the public realm. Each of the 35 finalists receives a complimentary copy of the group zine featuring all 35 selected photographers, along with an exhibition print of their selected image, per the organiser's press release. £25 covers one to ten images and you may submit as many times as you like at that rate; the organisers state that if selected there are no additional costs to exhibit, that all exhibition prints are produced by Rapid Eye Darkrooms on digital C-Type matte or gloss paper, and that the call is not-for-profit — a portion of fees goes to Not A Phase and Just Stop Oil, chosen by the judges, with the rest reinvested in the free photobook collection, the gallery programme and youth engagement. Eligibility is stated as wide open: emerging, established or amateur, any age, background and identity, from anywhere in the world. Entry is two steps and the form enforces the order: pay the £25 on the organiser's Squarespace store, then upload your images to the Google Form together with a screenshot of the payment receipt, which is a required field. Files are JPG at 2400px on the long edge, 300dpi, RGB, named forename_surname_photograph title_No., and selected photographers may be asked for a higher-resolution file for printing. Note on access: the gallery has no step-free access and is reached by 25 steps. — Deadline: October 26, 2026. Fee: £25/10 images. Prize: Exhibition + zine publication + mentoring + street gallery display.

item.title: Open Call for 2028 Exhibitions · Open Source Gallery
item.description: Open Source Gallery, a W.A.G.E.-certified 501(c)(3) in a renovated carriage house on 17th Street in Brooklyn, is choosing its 2028 exhibition programme by open call, and the terms are unusually good for a $15 application. The gallery invites proposals from “artists working in any medium and location, whose practices emphasize experimentation, sustainability, and social engagement” — photography is eligible, and the application form asks for Artistic Medium as free text rather than a pick-one list, so there is no medium gate. Selected artists receive artist fees calculated on the W.A.G.E. certification schedule, a production budget, and support from the gallery in planning, production and communications; this is a funded, produced exhibition rather than a wall rental. THE FEE IS WAIVABLE AND THE CALL PAGE IS THE ONE SURFACE THAT DOES NOT SAY SO: both the application form and the payment screen add “Open Source Gallery is a nonprofit art gallery, and our programs are always free or pay-what-you-can. The $15 Open Call fee is a donation that helps us continue to offer this programming. If the fee is cost-prohibitive for you, please email us… and we will work out an accommodation”, while the call page on the gallery's own site carries no waiver sentence at all. The $15 is paid through a dedicated donation link whose only preset amount is labelled “$15 (Required Application Fee)” — its single alternative is a box for increasing the figure, so $15 is a floor and not a range — with PayPal for applicants outside the US, and the payment confirmation is uploaded with the application. One PDF carries everything: a project proposal of no more than 1,000 words, an artist statement of no more than 250 words, a CV, and 10 to 15 images of recent work. The gallery shows conceptually-driven work from local and international artists on a monthly rotation alongside public programmes, and publishes its floor plan so proposals can be made to the actual room at 306 17th Street. Applicants will be notified in early 2027. No juror is named. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Exhibition + W.A.G.E. artist fee + production budget.

item.title: The Contemporary Print 2027 · PrintAustin
item.description: PrintAustin's 14th annual juried international exhibition, held with The Art Galleries at Austin Community College. READ THE MEDIUM RULE BEFORE YOU PAY: this is a printmaking survey and straight photography is excluded — “Solely digital and photographic prints are not eligible” — but photopolymer plate is one of the six techniques the organiser names as eligible, in its own words “lithography, relief, intaglio, silkscreen, photopolymer plate (i.e. SolarPlates), and monotype”, and “while non-traditional or digital output is accepted as a print element, submissions must utilize traditional print media as their primary technique.” So a photographer working in SolarPlate or photopolymer photogravure, or using a photographic element inside a work whose primary technique is printmaking, is eligible; a photographer submitting an inkjet or darkroom print is not. Any 2-D or 3-D work qualifies if printmaking is the sole or primary technique, including ceramics, sculpture, mixed media and artist books, and unless it is an installation nothing may exceed 72 inches in any direction. The jury is blind and the juror is Lauren Rosenblum, the Jensen Bryan Curator at The Print Center in Philadelphia, who has organised more than a dozen exhibitions there and previously held curatorial positions at the Philadelphia Museum of Art and the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston. THERE IS A FEE LADDER AND A WAIVER, NOT A SINGLE PRICE: $35 for three pieces, $10 instead of $35 for PrintAustin members, $10 for each additional piece over three up to six, and the organiser states “We have a limited number of waived registration fees regardless of membership status for artists in need should you be experiencing hardship”, available by email. Best in Show takes $500 in cash plus a podcast interview by Hello, Print Friend, in English or Spanish. TWO BARS SIT ONLY ON THE CaFE PROSPECTUS AND BIND ANYWAY: works shown in a past Contemporary Print may not be re-entered, and “Artists that were accepted into our 2025 The Contemporary Print are also ineligible--please join us in 2027!” — so a 2025 acceptee pays $35 for nothing. Work is consigned at a 70/30 split in the artist's favour, with PrintAustin responsible for safekeeping and insuring the work while it holds it and payment due within five weeks of a sale. Shipping is the artist's to arrange, the artist carries transit risk in both directions and must enclose a prepaid return label or the work will not be hung — but it is not unsubsidised: “Selected artists will receive a shipping stipend, courtesy of PrintAustin. Stipend amount minimum will be $50, exact amount TBD.” THE DELIVERY DATE IS NOT SETTLED ON ITS OWN RECORD: the terms say “by December 9, 2026”, the shipping block says only “in December”, and the organiser's own IMPORTANT DATES table says “JAN 9 Artwork due”; PrintAustin tells applicants to “Refer to direct correspondence from PrintAustin for updated info.” The exhibition runs at The Art Galleries at Austin Community College, 6101 Highland Campus Drive, with a reception on 27 February 2027. PrintAustin Collective is an artist-led nonprofit that runs an annual printmaking festival in Austin from 15 January to 15 February. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $500 + Exhibition.

item.title: Geographies: An Exploration of Places, Environments and Cultures · LoosenArt
item.description: LoosenArt's third open call running concurrently on its calls page, and the one it labels outright a “Call for Publication and Exhibition”. The brief asks what the places we inhabit and move through tell us today, and how landscapes, environments and cultures change the way we perceive boundaries: the publication will bring together works examining the relationships between the physical and the symbolic, human presence and the environment, and local experience and global processes, so that geographical, cultural, political and emotional boundaries become starting points for exploring territories, belonging and transformation through personal perspectives. ENTRY IS FREE AND THE CALL IS WORLDWIDE, and photography heads the organiser's own list of accepted media: “Photography, video, digital, visual design, visual data, installation, sculpture, painting.” Each artist may submit one to three works. The guaranteed outcome is publication — the works are selected for a new issue of the Issue Collective editorial project dedicated to this theme. The exhibition is a second, conditional stage: “Some of the works selected for publication will also be considered in a further selection for the LoosenArt Collective #2 exhibition, planned for 2027 in Milan, Rome or Cagliari, Italy” — the organiser has not fixed which city. Submission is through a single Google Form that LoosenArt shares across all of its live calls; a required “Select the call of interest” dropdown assigns the entry, and this call appears there as “Geographies - An Exploration Between Places, Environments and Cultures”, alongside Aesthetic Dynamics, Revelations and the closed Homo Technologicus. The form asks for name and surname, country, email, website, Instagram, how you heard about the opportunity, an artist statement of up to 70 words in English, and for each of up to three works a title, year of realisation, a file of no more than 5 MB, and a URL for video only. Files go out through SwissTransfer to the organiser's submissions address rather than uploading into the form. LoosenArt is a spare Google Sites presence whose contacts page names Antonio Muratore at an address in Quartu Sant'Elena, Sardinia; beyond the call text it publishes no further terms, and no charge of any kind is mentioned at any stage, on the call page or in the form. — Deadline: December 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: The Big Small Show 2026 · Drawing Rooms
item.description: Drawing Rooms closes its 25th anniversary year with The Big Small Show in what the gallery calls its eleventh year, a survey of work made in the past two years, hung across the nonprofit's expanded galleries — The Terrarium Gallery and The Alcove Gallery — inside the Mana Contemporary complex in Jersey City from 10 December 2026 to 17 January 2027. This is not a theme show: the organisers say outright “Is there a theme? No, just send work you would like to be considered, and the curator will identify and create groups/connections of concepts”, and the hang is built as a “curatorially-driven narrative” in which works “connect and interact with each other visually and conceptually”. ANY MEDIUM IS ACCEPTED AND PHOTOGRAPHY IS NAMED IN THE LIST: “painting or drawing on paper, canvas, or other media; sculpture, collage or textiles, photography or prints”. Small is preferred but not mandatory — work dropped off in Jersey City can be any size, while anything shipped must be no larger than 18 x 24 inches and travel flat in a rigid mailer or tube with return postage included. Prints may come unframed, framed or mounted on a cradled panel; if framed, the organisers ask for simple white, black or wood-tone frames no more than five inches larger than the image, and no floating acrylic. Entry is $35 for up to three images and there is no cash award: what comes back is the exhibition itself, a written curator's statement, a review, inclusion in the Artsy.net presentation and the organisers' newsletter and social channels, and consideration for Drawing Rooms' other programmes including The Art Project JC lobbies and its online Artsy exhibits through the year. ALL WORK MUST BE FOR SALE, with sales split 60% to the artist and 40% to Drawing Rooms, paid out within 30 days of the gallery receiving payment; work is insured from the moment it is in the gallery's possession. Whatever the gallery picks for Artsy stays listed there at the same 60/40 split for up to two months after the show closes, and entering commits the artist in advance to a collector discount of up to 10%, with the curator asking approval for anything deeper, to 20%. Notifications go out on 5 November 2026, hand delivery runs 20–22 November at Drawing Rooms and The Oakman, and mailed work must arrive by 23 November. AI is excluded: “Works must be original. No AI or reproductions of original works.” Drawing Rooms is a project of Victory Hall Inc., a 501(c)(3) running exhibitions, programmes and public art in the NJ/NY area since 2001, supported by the New Jersey State Council on the Arts. — Deadline: November 2, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Portrayed 5: A Juried National Exhibition of Portraits · d'Art Center
item.description: The fifth edition of d'Art Center's portrait show takes over the 2,200 sq ft Main Gallery of the Norfolk nonprofit, in the heart of the city's NEON arts district, from 9 January to 6 February 2027. The brief is narrow in subject and wide open in treatment: work must depict a human figure or a human face, and the organisers list Realism, Traditional, Abstract, Modern, Impressionist, Pop Art, Cubism, Surrealism, Contemporary and Street among the styles they want, “all styles of portraiture are welcome”. The call is national, all-medium and explicitly “open to all functional, non-functional, 2D, 3D, fine art, and fine art craft in ALL STYLES”, so photographic portraiture competes on the same wall as painting and sculpture; d'Art runs photography-specific shows in its Vault space in other months, so the medium is part of the programme rather than a loophole. Entry is $35 for three submissions — three images is the minimum, so one strong piece can be entered with detail shots or repeated — and each further work is $5 to a cap of ten. Gallery Director Amanda Bradley curates alongside a guest juror still to be named, and that juror picks the awards: $500, $300 and $150, paid by cheque within 45 days of the reception. Entrants must be 18 or older and living in the United States, work must have been made in the last eight years without the aid of an instructor or kit, weigh under 50 pounds and measure no more than 60 inches in its longest dimension, though Bradley can waive the size and weight limits by prior arrangement. Notifications go out by 5pm on 23 November 2026 and accepted work must reach Norfolk by 5pm on 19 December. Sales split 60/40 in the artist's favour, meaning a 40% gallery commission; artists pay shipping both ways and must include a prepaid FedEx or UPS return label (no USPS, no freight, no packing peanuts). The exhibition is also archived permanently on d'Art's online archive site, and the 14 January reception is streamed. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 works), $5 each additional. Prize: $500 / $300 / $150 + Exhibition.

item.title: The Deets: A National Exhibition of Intricate and Heavily Detailed Artworks · d'Art Center
item.description: d'Art Center fills The Vault — a historical bank vault inside the Norfolk nonprofit's building, kept as a small, close-up exhibition space — with “the art of meticulousness” from 9 January to 6 February 2027. The call wants work that rewards standing still: “artworks that emphasize intricate detail, layered complexity, and exquisite finesse”, from elaborate craftsmanship and subtle nuance to “unexpected elements revealed upon closer inspection”, so that visitors “slow down, look closer, and appreciate the artistry found in every mark, texture, and thoughtfully considered detail”. No medium is excluded and the eligibility text says only that “all styles and aesthetics are considered”; the scale of the room sets the real limit, with work capped at 36 inches in its longest dimension, a cap the Gallery Director can waive by prior arrangement depending on how much of the installation the artist takes on. For a photographer this is a show for the dense frame — fine-grain large-format detail, alternative-process surfaces, collage and hand-worked prints — rather than the single clean gesture. Entry is $30 for three submissions, three images being the minimum, with each further work $5 to a cap of ten. Gallery Director Amanda Bradley curates, and the awards are chosen by a panel of d'Art Center's own professional artists and staff: Best in Show takes $300. Entrants must be 18 or older and living in the United States, and work must have been made in the last eight years without the aid of an instructor or kit, and arrive hang- or pedestal-ready. Notifications go out by 5pm on 23 November 2026 and accepted work must reach Norfolk by 5pm on 19 December. Sales split 60/40 in the artist's favour, meaning a 40% gallery commission, and work may also be marked NFS; artists pay shipping both ways and must include a prepaid FedEx or UPS return label (no USPS, no freight, no packing peanuts). The reception on 14 January is shared with Portrayed in the main gallery, and the show is archived permanently online. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $30 (3 works), $5 each additional. Prize: $300 Best in Show + Exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Programme 2027 — Open Call · Foto Forum
item.description: Open call for the 2027 exhibition programme of Foto Forum in Bolzano — the South Tyrolean photography society's own gallery at Weggensteinstraße 3F, open Tuesday to Saturday with free admission, running exhibitions, photobook presentations, talks and workshops. The call is for a real exhibition slot, not a group hang: “Foto forum welcomes submissions from photographers, visual artists and other personalities working with photography”, and the organiser lists Exhibitions, Workshops and Talks/conferences as three separate submission categories with only Exhibitions carrying this deadline. NO THEME IS SET and no genre is excluded. WHAT AN EXHIBITION PROPOSAL MUST CONTAIN, verbatim from the guidelines: “8-20 images of the project (JPG)”, “Video links, if the project contains moving image work”, “Abstract of the project (PDF)”, “CV (PDF)”, “Installation proposal for our spaces (PDF)” and a “List of existing works, material, measures etc (PDF)” — so this wants a finished, installable body of work and a plan for the room, not single images. THERE IS NO ENTRY FEE: the guidelines enumerate the submission in full and never mention payment, and submission is by email to [email in contacts.json], with the organiser asking for “non-expiring file transfers with sharabke link that allows us to directly see hi-res images” and, if using Dropbox, a shared link rather than a folder invitation. NOTE THE ORGANISER'S OWN CUTOFF IS AMBIGUOUS: the page reads “Exhibitions (deadline 15th October 2026, midnight 00:00 am)”, and midnight 00:00 is the start of the 15th rather than its end, so treat 14 October as the safe date. No juror is named and no notification date is published. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Breakthrough ’27: A Sioux Falls Emerging Artist Showcase · Washington Pavilion Visual Arts Center
item.description: Free, no-jury showcase for emerging artists in the Everist Gallery at the Visual Arts Center inside the Washington Pavilion, Sioux Falls — eight galleries and South Dakota's largest art museum. Presented by Sioux Falls Stage & Gallery, which “invites emerging Sioux Falls-area artists to submit work for Breakthrough ’27: A Sioux Falls Emerging Artist Showcase, on view Dec. 18, 2026–March 28, 2027.” PHOTOGRAPHY IS NAMED, not implied: “all artistic mediums are welcome, including drawing, painting, sculpture, ceramics, photography, digital art and more.” THERE IS NO ENTRY FEE AND THERE IS NO SELECTION STEP — the museum states “there is no cost to participate, and all eligible artwork that meets the submission and content guidelines will be accepted while space remains available,” so the only competitive element is the awards. CASH AWARDS, presented at the Sioux Falls Stage & Gallery event and artist reception on Feb. 18: Best in Show $500, Breakthrough $200, Sioux Falls Spirit $200 — $900 in total, a figure summed here from the three the museum lists; no total is advertised. FOUR BINDING BARS: the artist must live within a 10-mile radius of Sioux Falls city limits; must never have had a solo exhibition at the Visual Arts Center; submits exactly one artwork; and that work must be no larger than 50 × 50 inches, no heavier than 75 pounds, and delivered ready to install. SUBMISSION IS IN PERSON ONLY — “artwork must be submitted in person. Online submissions will not be accepted.” Work and a completed paper form go to the Visual Arts Center front desk on the second floor on one of three Fridays: Oct. 23, Nov. 13 or Nov. 27, each 10 a.m.–4 p.m., with Nov. 27 marked “final opportunity.” NOTE THE CUTOFF IS 4 P.M., NOT MIDNIGHT. CONTENT GUIDELINES BIND because the show is open to visitors of all ages: work “must be appropriate for a general audience, including young children” and “should avoid explicit nudity or sexual content, graphic violence or disturbing imagery, profanity or overtly mature themes and overly political or religious content.” The museum publishes no AI policy for this call. — Deadline: November 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $900 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 2028 Solo Artist Application · The Art League
item.description: Application for a 2028 solo exhibition at The Art League gallery at 105 North Union Street in Alexandria, Virginia — inside the Torpedo Factory Art Center, and described by the gallery itself as "one of Washington's largest art galleries". THE GALLERY NAMES PHOTOGRAPHY EXPLICITLY in its media policy, which is the test worth checking before paying anything: "Photography: unique photographed images are acceptable. Photographers are encouraged, but not required, to process or print their own work. Unaltered reproductions of pre-existing artwork are not allowed (i.e., you may not take a photograph of a painting — yours or not — and submit it as an original)." WHAT THEY WANT: "artists who have a strong, cohesive, and exciting body of work expressing an aesthetic concept", and the stated aim, "whether we exhibit experimental or traditional works, is to adhere to the highest standards of quality. While we seek beautifully executed work, we also value work that is innovative, artwork that presents the artist's unique voice and engages the viewer intellectually, emotionally, and visually." THREE STAGES: five artwork images plus a detailed proposal, an artist statement and a résumé are submitted online; jurors review the applications and pick a group of finalists; the finalists physically drop off the same five works for in-person jurying, which happens without the artists present. APPLICATIONS RUN TWO YEARS AHEAD — this round is juried in November 2026 for shows in 2028. THREE ELIGIBILITY BARS, ALL BINDING: the artist must be a current Exhibiting Artist member of The Art League; the artist cannot have had a solo exhibit at The Art League in the last five years; and if selected, no more than one third of the works in the final show may have been shown in a juried solo exhibition within 50 miles of the gallery. COSTS: $50 to apply through Submittable, plus Exhibiting Artist membership at $115 for a new member or $105 on renewal — free for artists aged 23 and under under the gallery's Emerging Artist tier. NOTE WHAT THE ALL-INCLUSIVE MEMBERSHIP DOES NOT COVER: the $182 all-inclusive programme "covers Exhibiting Artist dues and all entry fees for exhibits held in the exhibiting year with the exception of solo exhibits, some specialty exhibits, and Gallery 75 fees", so the $50 is payable whichever membership you hold. AI GENERATED WORK IS NOT ACCEPTED, stated on the gallery's own media policy: "AI generated artwork is not accepted at this time." The 2028 jury panel is listed as "Jury Panel TBA" on the application itself. The gallery publishes its evaluation criteria in full — concept, the clarity of the statement, the detail of the proposal, cohesiveness of the body of work, technical skill and craftsmanship, professional presentation, and the formal elements — but on its own Solo Artist Jurying page, which has not been updated past the 2027 cycle, so read the criteria as the gallery’s standing ones and take every date and juror name from the application. Deadline Sunday 1 November 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $50 (Exhibiting Artist membership required, $115 new / $105 renewal; free for artists 23 and under). Prize: Solo exhibition in 2028.

item.title: Open Call AIR Lebensbogen 2027 — Industrieviertel · Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich
item.description: Free open call, no entry fee, for the Lebensbogen artist-in-residence programme in Grünbach am Schneeberg, Lower Austria, run by Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich with the Lebensbogen institution. ALL DISCIPLINES ON THE CALL, SEVEN NAMED ON THE DETAIL SHEET: the call block says the programme "lädt Künstlerinnen und Künstler aller Kunstsparten zu einem Arbeitsaufenthalt" — artists of every art form are invited to a working stay — while the linked detail PDF narrows that to a list, "Eingeladen sind Personen aus den Bereichen Bildende Kunst, Baukultur, Film, Musik, Literatur, Digitale Medien und Darstellende Kunst." Photography is named on neither surface and excluded on neither; it sits inside Bildende Kunst and Digitale Medien, and the CV asked for must carry a portrait photograph. WHAT THEY WANT: "künstlerische Vorhaben, die sich mit dem Ort, seiner Geschichte, der Natur oder den Lebensrealitäten der Menschen vor Ort auseinandersetzen" — projects engaging the place, its history, its nature or the lived realities of the people there, with "Begegnungen auf Augenhöhe" (encounters as equals) with residents and staff at the centre and a traceable place in the artist's own practice. Participatory and inclusive formats are expressly welcome. Lebensbogen's Christof Mikats frames it as space rather than a commission: "Kunst braucht Freiraum – um Neues auszuprobieren, verrückte Dinge zu machen und manchmal ganz neue Wege zu gehen." WHAT THE PROGRAMME COVERS: free accommodation, free board, use of available work and event rooms, introductions to the regional arts scene, the possibility of a closing presentation, and possible remuneration for participatory or inclusive formats ("mögliche Vergütung partizipativer oder inklusiver Formate" — possible, not guaranteed). WHAT THE ARTIST PAYS: travel to and from the residency and all working materials, stated plainly as "selbstständige Finanzierung von An- und Abreise sowie Arbeitsmaterialien". WHAT THE HOST IS, AND IT IS THE THING TO KNOW BEFORE APPLYING: the Lebensbogen is not a village studio but a residential and working community for people with disabilities and mental illness — "Der Lebensbogen bietet Menschen mit Behinderungen und psychischen Erkrankungen einen Lebensplatz, der Wohnen und Arbeiten miteinander verbindet." Participatory projects are welcome but expressly not therapeutic ("Partizipative, jedoch nicht therapeutische Projekte"), those are the ones that may carry a fee, and experience of artistic work with people with mental or physical impairments is stated as an advantage. 2027 is the pilot year; individuals or collectives may apply; the stay is in a fully equipped living container beside the workshop hall or a unit in the new residents’ centre, on an eight-hectare former mining and industrial site with hangars and a large workshop hall that projects may use. Residents are also required to attend a meeting day on site — attendance is "Voraussetzung für die Aufnahme in die finale Auswahlrunde", the precondition for reaching the final selection round — to engage with the site and the people there, and to leave behind a work or a documentation. STAY: 3 to 12 weeks, scheduled between April and October 2027; applicants state their preferred window and length. TWO ELIGIBILITY GATES, BOTH BINDING: artists and craftspeople with a connection to Lower Austria ("mit Niederösterreichbezug"), and membership of Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich, which is "für die Einreichung Voraussetzung" — a precondition for submitting, not merely for the stay. THE MEMBERSHIP IS CHEAP AND OPEN, NOT JURIED: the association publishes its "JÄHRLICHER MITGLIEDSBEITRAG" as €25 for "Künstler:innen/ Einzelpersonen" (€50 for associations, institutions and groups, €100 for businesses, €160 for municipalities), applied for through an online form, effective on payment and cancellable in writing each year. Submission is one PDF of at most 8 MB with a CV carrying a portrait photograph, a portfolio, a short description of the project and the requested dates, sent by email to the Industrieviertel office. Deadline Tuesday 1 December 2026. No notification date is published on either surface. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free (Kulturvernetzung NÖ membership required, €25/year individual). Prize: Free 3–12 week residency + accommodation and board.

item.title: In Character · L.A. Photo Curator
item.description: Open call from L.A. Photo Curator on character, identity and presence — "photographs that reveal personality, identity, presence, and the many ways people inhabit the world." The brief is deliberately wide: "A character study can focus on someone else — or on yourself. It may be direct or subtle, staged or spontaneous. Character can emerge through a face, a gesture, clothing, posture, surroundings, relationships, or the small details that tell us something about a person." The curator is explicit that the sitter need not be fully visible: "The subject does not have to look directly at the camera, or even be fully seen." Juried by Laurie Freitag, who founded the platform eleven years ago. EVERY ENTRANT IS SHOWN: "All entrants included in the online group exhibition (with artist statement, bio, and website)". First place receives a solo online exhibition, an online article including a Q&A with the juror's responses, and their image on the L.A. Photo Curator splash page for one month; selected work is also considered for Top 40 Images of the Year and the Photographer of the Year title. ONE UNUSUAL RETURN: "One participating photographer will be invited to serve as a Guest Juror alongside Laurie Freitag for a future L.A. Photo Curator competition." Entry is $25 for either three or six images — exactly those numbers, not "up to" — paid by PayPal or card through the page's Buy Now button, then emailed as a ZIP of JPEGs at 1024 pixels on the longest side, 72 DPI, under 1 MB each. A limited number of fee waivers are available on request. Five per cent of entry fees goes to Best Friends Animal Society and another five per cent to a charity the winner chooses. Open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional. Deadline November 1, 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Solo online exhibition.

item.title: Open Call M-ZONE 2027 — Weinviertel · Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich
item.description: Free open call, no entry fee, for two curated exhibitions in the M-ZONE — a roughly 150 m² hall in Mistelbach, Lower Austria, that sits between two of the region's major institutions, the nitsch museum and MAMUZ. 2027 starts a new cooperation between Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich, the nitsch museum, MAMUZ and the Province of Lower Austria, and the two shows it produces are what this call fills. WHAT THEY ARE LOOKING FOR: "künstlerische und kuratorische Konzepte, die aktuelle Fragen aufgreifen und eine eigenständige Haltung entwickeln" — artistic and curatorial concepts that take up current questions and develop a position of their own. The organisers ask for projects that treat the hall as more than wall space: "Willkommen sind Projekte, die die M-ZONE nicht nur als Ausstellungsfläche verstehen, sondern den Raum in ihre inhaltliche und formale Entwicklung einbeziehen" — projects that draw the room itself into their conceptual and formal development. New and existing projects both qualify, the existing ones "adaptiert oder weiterentwickelt" for this space. NO MEDIUM IS NAMED AND NONE IS EXCLUDED: the call asks for exhibition concepts rather than a medium, so a photographic project with a spatial idea competes on the same terms as any other — but equally, photography is not singled out as welcome, and an applicant is pitching a show, not submitting images. WHO CAN APPLY: "Einzelpersonen, Kollektive & kuratorische Teams mit Niederösterreichbezug (z.B. Wohnort, Arbeitsort)" — individuals, collectives and curatorial teams with a Lower Austria connection, residence or workplace given as the examples. No membership in Kulturvernetzung is required for this call, unlike two of the organiser's other current open calls. WHAT A SELECTED PROJECT GETS: a four-week exhibition and a total project budget of €3,000. The venue's own page describes the space as "rund 150 m² Raum für Kultur, Kreativität und Feste – mit moderner Infrastruktur". HOW IT IS JUDGED: "Die Auswahl erfolgt durch eine Fachjury aus Vertreterinnen und Vertretern der beteiligten Institutionen sowie externen Jurymitgliedern" — a specialist jury of representatives of the participating institutions plus external members, assessing "künstlerische Qualität | räumliche und konzeptionelle Schlüssigkeit" (artistic quality, spatial and conceptual coherence). No juror is named. WHAT TO SEND, in one PDF of at most 8 MB, by email only: the exhibition concept including images, portfolios and CVs of everyone involved, and contact details with an email address and phone number. TIMELINE: entries close Monday 2 November 2026, the jury sits in November 2026, results are announced in January 2027, and the two exhibitions run March/April and July/August 2027 with exact dates still to be set. The whole call is published in German. — Deadline: November 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €3,000 project budget + four-week exhibition.

item.title: Come In! Galerie Waidhofen/Ybbs — Open Call 2027 · Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich
item.description: Free open call, no entry fee, for six multi-week solo exhibitions in 2027 at the Come In! Galerie — a roughly 30 m² exhibition room in the Impulsquartier in Waidhofen an der Ybbs run specifically for artists under 29, by Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich as part of the province's Come On! youth-culture programme. THE OFFER IS PAID, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT UNUSUAL FOR AN AGE-LIMITED FIRST-SHOW CALL: a fee of €500 and up to €500 in material-cost reimbursement ("Honorar € 500 und bis zu € 500 Materialkostenersatz"), support for the exhibition and the opening, optional guidance on exhibition design and installation from experienced curators ("Auf Wunsch Begleitung bei der Ausstellungsgestaltung und beim Aufbau durch erfahrene Kuratorinnen"), inclusion in an annual publication that collects the year's shows, and introductions to the regional art scene. WHO IT IS FOR, in the gallery's own second person: "Du bist zwischen 14 und 29 Jahre alt und stehst am Beginn Deiner künstlerischen Laufbahn" — aged 14 to 29 and at the start of your artistic career — plus "einen persönlichen, künstlerischen oder beruflichen Bezug zu Niederösterreich", a personal, artistic or professional connection to Lower Austria. No membership is required. ONE CONDITION WORTH READING BEFORE APPLYING: you must be present in person at the gallery during opening hours on the first weekend of your exhibition (Friday 16:00–19:00, Saturday 10:00–13:00, Sunday 15:00–18:00), so this is not a send-and-forget show. NO MEDIUM IS NAMED, in either direction: the call asks for "Deine Werke" and a "Werkübersicht für die geplante Ausstellung (Fotos oder Links)", so a photographic body of work is as admissible as any other, but photography is not singled out as welcome. HOW IT IS JUDGED: "Die Bewerbungen werden von einer Fachjury beurteilt" — a specialist jury, its six members named not in the call block but on the gallery's own page at kulturvernetzung.at/de/come-in-galerie/ — selecting six artists on "künstlerische Qualität, Motivation, Potenzial und Engagement in Hinblick auf die Realisierbarkeit einer Ausstellung" (artistic quality, motivation, potential, and commitment measured against whether the exhibition can actually be realised). WHAT TO SEND, by email: a portfolio or work overview for the exhibition you are planning (photos or links), a CV focused on your artistic work so far, and an artist statement saying why you want to exhibit and what inspires you. THE 2027 SLOTS ARE ALREADY DATED: 19 February–14 March, 2–25 April, 21 May–13 June, 3–26 September, 1–24 October, and 12 November–5 December 2027. The call is published in German, and receipt of an application is confirmed. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500 + up to €500 materials + Publication.

item.title: Fresh Eyes Gallery — Call for Submissions · ViewPoint Gallery
item.description: Rolling, free call for the Fresh Eyes series at ViewPoint Gallery, a photographer-run fine-art photography gallery founded in 2000 on the Bedford Highway in Halifax Regional Municipality, Nova Scotia. FRESH EYES IS A MONTHLY SLOT, NOT A GROUP SHOW: "Fresh Eyes is a monthly exhibition series at ViewPoint Gallery designed to showcase the work of Maritime photographers", and the space is a defined 5' × 5' wall — "You get to decide how you would like to make use of it." That is small, and it is the whole point: one photographer at a time, with the layout left to them. NO FEE AND NO COMMISSION, which is unusual enough to state plainly: "There is no fee to exhibit and, in the event of sales, the Gallery does not charge commission" — the only deduction is a 10% handling charge on credit or debit sales. WHAT THE GALLERY DOES: "We'll take care of printing your wall cards and artist statement/bio", and "Your show will be highlighted on our website and social media". WHAT THE ARTIST DOES: "All works should be printed and prepared for hanging by the artist." WHO CAN APPLY: "All artists must be from Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, or New Brunswick" — the three Maritime provinces, and nowhere else. WHAT TO SEND, by email with "Exhibition Chair" in the subject line: an artist statement about you as a photographer, a statement of exhibition intent saying what you intend to exhibit and why, a very brief bio, and 2–3 digital images. All images must meet the gallery's published content guidelines, which sit on their own page. THERE IS NO DEADLINE AND NO ANNOUNCED CYCLE — the call is open-ended, which is why it is listed as continuous; the gallery's separate guest-exhibition route asks for submissions at least three months ahead of an opening, so planning that far out is the gallery's habit. ONE THING TO SEPARATE THIS FROM THE GALLERY'S OTHER DOOR: ViewPoint's solo guest exhibitions in the main gallery carry a $150 non-refundable exhibition fee plus shipping and catering at the artist's expense. Fresh Eyes does not. Note also that the gallery states it cannot insure work on display. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Monthly solo exhibition slot, no sales commission.

item.title: ContemporaryIdentities Issue #31
item.description: Free open call for the 31st issue of ContemporaryIdentities, "an independent quarterly international online magazine covering contemporary art from around the world" whose stated focus is "to showcase and promote experimental and progressive contemporary art through short art reviews from international scholars, art writers and art critics". Selected artworks are featured in the next issue alongside the magazine's invited criticism and artist interviews. THE MEDIA DOOR IS WIDE OPEN AND SAID SO: "Visual artists in any disciplines are welcome to submit artworks in any medium for our 31st Issue" — photography is not singled out but it is not excluded by any medium restriction either, and the call carries no theme. WHO RUNS IT: editors-in-chief and founders Sara Berti and Dr. Elham Shafaei, with a curatorial board of Dr. Izmer Ahmad and Dr. Zoltán Somhegyi; the magazine states it has been chosen for the Arts and Society database, in partnership with the Conseil International de la Philosophie et des Sciences Humaines (CIPSH), UNESCO-MOST, The Global Chinese Art, Culture and Society (GCACS) and Mémoire de l'Avenir. WHAT TO SEND: three to five high-resolution images with each work's title, year, medium and size, plus an artist statement and a short bio, by email. ONE WARNING THE MAGAZINE GIVES ITSELF: "We are not able to respond to each individual. We will only contact the successful applicant" — so silence after the deadline is the expected outcome for everyone not selected, not a lost email. Applicants must be 18 or over. The cutoff is stated in the magazine's own timezone, UTC+04:00, which runs ahead of European and American clocks — a European entrant effectively loses the last part of 15 October. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: PhotoWork Junior Fellowship 2027
item.description: Six-month one-to-one mentorship for early-career US photographers working in the post-documentary tradition, running January–June 2027, with a $1,000 production stipend and $2,000 of in-kind photographic services. Six Junior Fellows are chosen by a jury of industry colleagues and each is paired with an established photographer the foundation judges the best fit for that fellow's work and needs; the named mentor pool "include[s], but [is] not limited to, Barbara Bosworth, Kelli Connell, Lois Conner, Carolyn Drake, Doug DuBois, Rahim Fortune, Ron Jude, Andrea Modica, Kristine Potter, Irina Rozovsky, and Bryan Schutmaat". WHAT THE SIX MONTHS LOOK LIKE: each fellow develops a photographic project of their own choosing through monthly one-to-one online critique sessions with their mentor, discussing progress, refining artistic vision, and strengthening "both written and oral articulation of their work". On top of that come tailored sessions on post-production and professional practice, a professional-practices session with Executive Director Sasha Wolf, periodic group meetings to build a peer network, and an online profile on the PhotoWork Foundation site. WHAT IT PAYS: a $1,000 USD stipend "to aid in the production of work" and $2,000 USD of in-kind photographic services with picturehouse + thesmalldarkroom. EVEN NOT WINNING HAS A PAYOUT: the ten shortlisted applicants each receive a portfolio review with Sasha Wolf, and their application fee is waived for the next Junior Fellowship cycle. THE FELLOWSHIP IS AIMED AT ARTISTS OUTSIDE THE ACADEMIC PIPELINE — it supports photographers "regardless of formal training or completed arts education" and offers "a space for education and experimentation beyond traditional academic pathways" — and the ineligibility list is correspondingly specific: you are out if you are currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate degree programme, hold an arts-related graduate degree, have current gallery representation or have had multiple gallery exhibitions, or have more than five years' professional experience as a photographer. Applicants must be a US citizen or Permanent Resident, at least 18, have a project with image-making central to it, and be able to commit at least 12 hours of online mentoring plus project time across the six months. THE APPLICATION IS SUBSTANTIAL: an artist bio (2,000 characters), an artist statement (2,000), a statement of intent covering how a mentorship helps you now and what you will make (9,000), a history of relevant experience (1,200), a description of your artistic process as it relates to the submitted images (1,200), two character references who need not be arts-related and may not be family, and 20–25 images from the project you intend to advance — the foundation wants work that "demonstrates both their understanding of photographic language and their ability to edit a cohesive series of images". Fellows are announced in December 2026. The foundation states it does not discriminate on race, religion, colour, national origin, sex including pregnancy and reproductive health decisions, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age or disability status. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $35 (waiver available on request). Prize: $1,000 stipend + $2,000 in-kind services.

item.title: SOMETHING NEW — October 2026 Open Call · Thirdplat
item.description: Free monthly open call from Thirdplat, an independent online platform that publishes work against a rolling monthly theme and keeps it in a permanent public archive. Photography is named outright among the welcomed forms: "Whether manifested as moving image, photography, writing, craft, sound, performance, or cross-disciplinary work, Thirdplat welcomes original, respectful creations directly to our open global platform." THE THEME is an inquiry into consequence rather than novelty — "SOMETHING NEW is not simply a celebration of novelty, but an inquiry into impact: when something new enters our lives, what does it change?" The platform asks for work reflecting on "one new presence in your life, community, or practice, and the trace it has left behind", and lists the pressures it has in mind: pandemics shifting human distance, displacement turning home into a portable memory, climate rewriting landscapes, AI redefining authorship. The "new" may be "a place, relationship, technology, loss, habit, identity or unfamiliar way of seeing", and responses "may be personal, social, documentary, fictional or experimental". THIS IS NOT A COMPETITION and the platform says so plainly: "Thirdplat is not a conventional competition or juried exhibition. We treat submission as publication rather than audition." Accepted work is published directly, subject to the platform's content guidelines, and becomes part of that month's online exhibition and the archive. WHAT AN ARTIST GETS: a public page for the work, an artist profile "that can develop into an ongoing record of their practice", a direct shareable link, and placement alongside other readings of the same theme — the platform's stated aim is to "give emerging and independent creative work a place where it can remain visible beyond a single post, exhibition or deadline". Entry is free, up to three works, one entry per artist, files up to 50MB each as JPG, PNG, TIFF, MOV or MP4, and it is open worldwide: "Creators from around the world are invited to show us what entered their world, what it changed and what it left behind." AI IS ACCEPTED WITH A DUTY TO DISCLOSE, in the Terms of Use rather than on the call page: "Thirdplat accepts thoughtful engagement with artificial intelligence, digital systems and emerging creative tools. If artificial intelligence has materially generated or transformed a submitted work, you should describe its role honestly." THE RIGHTS CLAUSE IS CLEAN: the artist keeps copyright, and the licence granted to THIRDPLAT LTD is "non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free" and scoped "only for operating, presenting, archiving and promoting Thirdplat, its open calls and participating artists", with removal available on request. TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE SPENDING TIME ON IT. The terms qualify the no-audition promise — "Submission does not guarantee selection, publication, exhibition, promotion or any other particular outcome", and Thirdplat "may decide which works are selected, featured, published, archived or displayed". And the archive is nearly empty: the platform’s own content index returns two published artworks in total across its whole life, not two this month, alongside three posted open calls. TWO FURTHER THEMES ARE ALREADY POSTED on the platform's own open-calls index — 2026-11 THE THIRD SPACE: CULTURAL HYBRIDITY and 2026-12 REFLECTION: AI AND US — so a photographer who misses this window has a monthly one behind it. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online publication + artist profile + archive placement.

item.title: Animalia: Our Shared World · PhotoPlace Gallery
item.description: PhotoPlace Gallery's January call for photographs about the diversity of animal life — "From beloved companions and backyard visitors to wildlife, birds, insects, reptiles, amphibians, marine life, and the countless creatures that inhabit our planet". The gallery asks for work that explores "the beauty, character, behavior, and relationships of animals in all their forms", whether that is life in the wild, intimate moments with domestic animals, or the tangle of relationships between animals, people and the natural world, and states outright that "All photographic genres and processes are encouraged." THE JUROR is Wendi Schneider, the American artist behind States of Grace, an ongoing series begun in 2012 of hand-gilded photographs printed on translucent vellum or Japanese kozo and gilded on the verso with precious metals; her work is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, the Center for Creative Photography, the New Orleans Museum of Art, the Royal Photographic Society, the Memphis Brooks Museum of Art, the Asheville Art Museum and Auburn University Libraries Special Collections, and she sits on the Advisory Council of the Colorado Photographic Arts Center. WHAT GETS TAKEN: up to 35 photographs for the Middlebury, Vermont gallery and roughly 40 more for the Online Gallery, and the gallery is explicit that the two tiers are treated the same — "Online Gallery selections receive the same catalog inclusion, permanent website archive, and promotional opportunities as Exhibition Gallery selections." Every selected artist gets the exhibition catalogue, permanent placement on the PhotoPlace site, promotion through the gallery's channels with a link back to their own website, and eligibility for exhibition awards; the gallery's own page does not put a figure on those awards. THE DATES: entries opened 6 October 2026, selections are announced 23 November 2026, prints for the Middlebury gallery are due 18 December 2026, and the show hangs 1–30 January 2027 with an opening reception on Friday 1 January, 4–7 pm. BEYOND THE FEE this is a print-and-ship show for the 35 gallery selections; the gallery runs in-house printing and display services that international artists are told they may use "to reduce shipping expenses", and notes international return shipping "may involve additional costs". JURYING IS BLIND — files are renamed and jurors see no names. Submissions are open worldwide: "We warmly welcome submissions from photographers around the world." Work accepted into a previous PhotoPlace exhibition may not be resubmitted for three years from that show's opening date, and there is no cap on how many images one photographer may enter; files are JPG, max 5 MB, about 2100 px on the long side. — Deadline: November 9, 2026. Fee: $39 (5 images) + $6 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: 2027 National Juried Exhibition · The Delaplaine Arts Center
item.description: The Delaplaine's annual all-media national open, hung at its Frederick, Maryland arts centre from May 1 to July 11, 2027, with the juror's talk and award announcement on opening day. Photography is named outright on the organiser's own page for this exhibition: "All media are eligible, including but not limited to: painting, printmaking, photography, ceramics, drawing, installation, and sculpture", and the platform prospectus repeats the openness from the other direction — "There are no theme, size or media requirements or restrictions for this exhibition." THE 2027 JUROR is Timothy Paul Brown, Director of IA&A at Hillyer, the contemporary art centre of International Arts & Artists in Washington DC, with more than 25 years across contemporary art, museum education and exhibitions; he holds a Master's in Museum Education and a BFA from the University of the Arts, Philadelphia. JUDGING RUNS IN TWO ROUNDS and only the first is remote: the juror works virtually through the entry portal to decide what gets in, then judges the awards IN PERSON after the work is installed — so the cash decisions are made from the prints on the wall, not from JPEGs. THE MONEY: $1,000 first place, $500 second, $250 third and $125 honourable mention, itemised identically on the organiser's page and the prospectus. WHAT IT COSTS BEYOND THE FEE: this is a ship-or-drive show. Accepted work must be hand delivered or received at 40 S. Carroll Street, Frederick between Monday 19 and Sunday 25 April 2027, shipped work must include a prepaid return label, and everything must stay on the wall for the full ten weeks; pick-up is 4–5 pm on Sunday 11 July or 9 am–5 pm on Monday 12 July 2027, and work left later "may be disposed of at the Delaplaine's discretion". Work must have been made within the past two years and must not have been shown at the Delaplaine before. Two-dimensional wall work need not be framed but must arrive wired to a professional standard for the gallery's hanging system — the prospectus is emphatic that sawtooth hangers and any kind of tape will be refused. Work may be entered for sale or marked NFS — "Artists are not required to offer work for sale" — but if it sells the Delaplaine retains 30% commission from a non-member and 20% from a member, a ladder that appears only in the platform record's Legal Agreement section and nowhere on the gallery's own page. THE ORGANISER'S OWN PAGE FOR THIS EXHIBITION STILL CARRIES THE 2026 EDITION — 2026 juror Kyle Hackett, a March 2026 deadline, a May–July 2026 run — and the Opportunities index above it still lists the National Juried Exhibition under "Call for entry coming fall of 2026". Entries nonetheless opened on 17 September 2026 and the platform record is live, so every 2027 figure here is taken from that record, not from the gallery's unrefreshed page.
